NAO EXECUTADO: arraste real, persistencia da posicao e WhatsApp/GOWA conectado com midias reais.

Apos compilar, validar fotos, figurinhas (incluindo animadas), audio/video, conexao com Codex,
permissoes, centralizacao, multiplos monitores e preservacao dos dados antes de distribuir o hotfix.

A midia usa GET /message/{message_id}/download do GOWA e o arquivo statics/media no mesmo gateway,
com redirecionamentos/proxy desativados, tipos permitidos e limite de 24 MiB.

> **Versão personalizada:** melhorias no WhatsApp, chat como tela inicial, posição horizontal, nome configurável e hotfixes para Windows. Veja [como usar e atualizar](LEIA-ME-ATUALIZACOES.md). Baseado no Coucou original, com créditos e licenças preservados.
# Coucou **A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows and Linux — and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. And now on your phone too: iPhone and Android.** Approve permissions, watch your agents work, drop a file, chat with Claude — all without leaving what you're doing. Walk away from your Mac and Mochi follows you to your iPhone: Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, widgets, Siri. **New in 0.4: Coucou is a real Mac app.** Hold a key anywhere, speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, like Wispr Flow — free, open source, and offline with Parakeet. Record your calls without a bot in the meeting and get the transcript, the summary and the to-dos. [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Louis-CFM/coucou?filter=v*&label=version&color=0A84FF)](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou/releases) ![macOS 15+](https://img.shields.io/badge/macOS-15%2B-black?logo=apple) ![iOS 18+](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-18%2B-black?logo=apple) ![Android 11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android-11%2B-3DDC84?logo=android&logoColor=white) ![Windows 10/11](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-10%2F11-0078D4?logo=windows&logoColor=white) ![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linux-AppImage%20%7C%20deb%20%7C%20rpm-FCC624?logo=linux&logoColor=black) ![Swift 6](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-6-F05138?logo=swift&logoColor=white) ![SwiftUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/SwiftUI-native-0A84FF) ![Tauri 2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tauri-2-FFC131?logo=tauri&logoColor=black) ![Code: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-MIT-green) ![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Louis-CFM/coucou?style=social)
--- ## Why Some studios showed off gorgeous notch companions… and never let anyone use them. **Coucou is the open version.** Every line of code is open source under the MIT License: read it, fork it, learn from it. The Coucou name, Mochi and the sounds stay © Louis Raillé (see [License](#license)). Meet **Mochi**: a soft little squircle with big eyes that pops out of your notch, waves hello, follows your cursor with its eyes, gets annoyed when you poke it (and dizzy if you insist), and tells you the moment Claude Code needs you. ## Coucou on the Mac: dictation, notes, one window
Since 0.4, Coucou has its own window and sits in the Dock. On the left, **Flow** — everything about your voice — and **Notch**, all the settings of the island. *(macOS, GitHub build)* - 🎙️ **Flow dictation** — hold a key anywhere on the Mac (right ⌥ by default, or fn, right ⌘ or right ⌃), speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, in any app. Two quick taps for hands-free (or one, with a setting), Esc to cancel, ⌃⌘V to paste the last one again. Your clipboard gets back what it held. - 💊 **The pill** — a small see-through pill at the bottom of the screen (or on its left or right edge). Hover it for a toolbar: dictate, record a call, open Coucou. While you speak, Mochi listens and nine dots follow your voice. - 🦜 **Parakeet, offline** — run NVIDIA's Parakeet on your Mac's Neural Engine through [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio): more accurate, 25 languages, nothing leaves your Mac. One click to download (about 650 MB), Apple silicon only. Until then the Mac's own recognition is used. - ✍️ **Your words, your way** — a dictionary of names Coucou always spells right, replacements, snippets (say a short phrase, paste a whole text), and an optional clean-up by Claude, on your Claude plan through Claude Code or with your own key: as said, natural or polished, per app. - 📝 **Notetaker** — click Record a call: Coucou records your microphone and what your Mac plays, no bot joins the call. Then you get the transcript person by person, a summary, the key points and the to-dos, written by Claude with your key or by Apple Intelligence on your Mac. The audio is deleted once the transcript is written. Tell the people in the call that you record. - 📊 **Statistics** — words dictated, time saved, words per minute, days in a row and the apps you dictate in. Counted on your Mac, never sent anywhere.
Flow dictation and the Notetaker are on the Mac for now; Windows and Linux are next. ## Features - 🤖 **Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Muse Code, OpenCode, Amp, Hermes, Claude Desktop and other agents, live** — see every session in your notch: what it reads, edits and runs, step by step. Tag a hook payload with `coucou_agent` to give any agent its own pill (see [`docs/AGENTS.md`](docs/AGENTS.md)). Finished? Mochi does a happy little jump. - See what Claude is editing, live in the notch: each file modification shows the file name and +N −M counts in the ticker, tap to read the full diff - ✅ **Approve and answer from the notch** — Claude Code permission requests show up with **Allow / Deny / Always**; `AskUserQuestion` prompts show the choices right in the notch (single or multi-select, up to 4 questions). One click, or "Reply in terminal" to fall back to the CLI. Codex also gets Allow / Deny. - 🧑‍💻 **Jump to the right terminal** — open the exact terminal window of a session *(macOS)*. - 💬 **Chat with Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot, or a local model (Ollama / LM Studio)** — click the model name above the chat box to switch provider and pick a model. Cloud providers use your own API key; local providers connect to a server running on your Mac. **No API key? Use your subscription**: switch it on in Settings → Chat and the chat goes through the official terminal tool you already pay for, signed in with your own account — Claude Code, Antigravity CLI or Gemini CLI, Codex CLI (ChatGPT), Cursor CLI or GitHub Copilot CLI *(GitHub build, Windows, Linux)*. *(Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Moonshot and local models: macOS)* - 📈 **Portfolio pill** *(macOS)* — track your crypto across 16 networks (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, BNB, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Dogecoin, Litecoin, TRON, XRP, Cardano, Cosmos, NEAR) and 5 exchanges (Binance, OKX, Bybit, Kraken, Coinbase) in the notch. Live balances, 7-day sparklines and 24-hour price change per holding. Read-only API keys for exchanges, public addresses for wallets — nothing leaves your Mac. - 📊 **Claude plan usage** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — a small pill in the notch header shows your 5-hour and weekly Claude plan limits. Enable it from Settings → Agents → Plan usage. Pro and Max plans only. - 📊 **Codex plan usage** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — a Codex pill next to it shows your Codex limits and how many free resets you have left, read from the Codex CLI. Turn it on in Settings → Agents → Plan usage. - 📋 **Declare the tools you use** — open Settings → Active pills and pick your main workspace tool (VS Code, Cursor, Codex or Antigravity), then toggle up to 4 more: Gemini CLI, Anthropic, Google AI, OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio and service integrations *(macOS)*. - ✉️ **Mail in the notch** *(macOS GitHub build: Apple Mail; Windows: classic Outlook)* — search every inbox and filter (Unread, Important, Today), read a message and act on it: reply, mark as read, important, junk. Coucou → Mail sorts new messages for you with your rules, banned words and VIPs, every action listed with Undo; nothing is ever deleted. Turn on **Mail** in the chat and the AI can prepare a plan — sorting, reply drafts, a mail merge with each recipient's page of a PDF — that runs only when you click Run. - 📎 **Drop a file on the notch** — Mochi turns into a box and swallows it, then ask a question about it or send it by email *(email: macOS, Mail.app)*. - 🖥️ **Mochi on the desktop** — drag Mochi out of the island to set him loose on your desktop: he floats as a 120 pt companion, follows your cursor, wears his outfit, reacts to alerts by flying home and flying back, and comes back where you left him on next launch. - 🪟 **Drag Mochi onto any window** — attach that window as context for Claude *(macOS)*. - 🔌 **Integrations** — Stripe payments, n8n workflows, GitHub (open PRs, reviews requested, CI status), Vercel deployments, Resend emails, Notion, Cal.com. Each one gets its own little colored Mochi. - 🎵 **Apple Music pill** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — add the Apple Music pill in Settings → Active pills to see what's playing and control playback from the notch; Mochi dances while it plays. - 🎧 **Spotify pill** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — add the Spotify pill in Settings → Active pills: album cover, title and artist, a progress bar you drag to seek, play/pause, previous/next, shuffle, repeat and volume, right from the notch; Mochi dances while it plays. - 👗 **Dress Mochi up** — right-click him for the wardrobe. He also dresses up for the seasons on his own. - ⌨️ **Keyboard shortcuts** — open the chat, jump to an alert or a terminal, switch pills, mute, send Mochi to the desktop or open the wardrobe from anywhere; all customizable in Settings → Shortcuts. - 🎭 **A real character** — idle breathing, blinks, eyes on a sphere that follow your mouse, emotes, 28 handcrafted sounds, a greeting on launch. - 🔊 **Your own sounds** *(macOS)* — drop a file named like one of Mochi's sounds (`finish.wav`, `approval.mp3`…) in Settings → General → Sound → **Open sounds folder** to replace it. - 🗣️ **« OK Coucou »** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — talk to Mochi like Jarvis. Say « OK Coucou », then ask: « how much did I make on Stripe today? », « swap GitHub for Stripe », « play some Daft Punk », « who won the game last night? », « send an email to Enzo to tell him the image is ready ». Claude is the brain (your own Anthropic API key, set in Settings → Chat); speech recognition runs on your Mac, and only your words and the data Coucou reads to answer go to Anthropic, never audio. Mochi listens, thinks and answers out loud; emails open in the notch and leave only when you click Send. Settings → Voice. - 🎙️ **Dictate in the chat** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — click the mic next to the chat field and talk in any of your languages (Coucou picks the one you spoke, or right-click the mic to choose); speech recognition runs on your Mac when it supports it. - ↘️ **The notch or a corner** *(macOS, GitHub build)* — put Coucou in any corner of the screen: drag Mochi there, or Settings → General → Display → Position. A small tile with Mochi at rest; open, the other pills sit on a quarter circle around him. - 🔎 **Search the settings** — type in the Coucou window's sidebar to find any setting *(macOS GitHub build, Windows, Linux)*. - 🫥 **Invisible when idle** — hides away when nothing is running, peeks out when you hover the notch (the top edge of the screen on Windows and Linux). - 🖥️ **Any Mac, notch or not** — on an iMac, a Mac mini, or a MacBook with its lid closed on an external display, Mochi sits in a small bar at the top of the screen. With several displays, pick his screen in Settings → General, or let him follow your mouse *(macOS)*. - 📱 **Coucou on iPhone** — your sessions, approvals and services in your pocket, with Live Activities, widgets and Siri. See [Coucou on iPhone](#coucou-on-iphone). - 🤖 **Coucou for Android** — your agents, approvals with your fingerprint, questions, chat and home-screen widgets on an Android phone, linked to Coucou on Windows or Linux over your Wi-Fi. By [@Rhytam23](https://github.com/Rhytam23). See [Coucou for Android](#coucou-for-android). - 📅 **Weekly recap** *(macOS)* — every Monday morning Coucou shows a summary of the past week: time coding, sessions, files, lines changed, commands, permissions, top agent and project, busiest day and longest session. Share it as a 1080 × 1920 image with Mochi — project names optional. All local, no sync. - 🌍 **16 languages** — English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, हिन्दी, Español, العربية, Français, বাংলা, Português, Русский, Bahasa Indonesia, Deutsch, Türkçe, ไทย, 한국어, 日本語. Pick one in Settings → General → Language; Traditional Chinese and Thai are on the Mac only for now. Community translations welcome. - 🔒 **Private by design** — no telemetry, no account. Keys live in your macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or Linux Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet). The app only talks to the services you plug in (and, once you agree, to GitHub's releases API to tell you about new versions). ## Coucou on iPhone The Mac app does the work; the iPhone app keeps you in the loop when you step away. It goes as far into the Apple ecosystem as a dev tool can:
- 🏝️ **Live Activity and Dynamic Island** — lock your Mac while an agent works and Mochi moves to your iPhone's Lock Screen and Dynamic Island with the agent's state, then comes back to the notch when you unlock. **Allow** or **Deny** a permission right from the Lock Screen, without opening the app. - 🔔 **Notifications you can act on** — Allow, Review or Deny a permission, pick an answer to Claude's question, or reply to a finished agent, straight from the notification. - 🔐 **Face ID on every Allow** — nothing runs on your Mac without your explicit tap; your Mac only applies a decision meant for the exact request it is waiting on. - 💬 **Talk to your agents** — follow each session live (steps, diffs, the last turn), answer questions, and send the next instruction to your Mac by text or voice. - 🧩 **Widgets, Control Center, Siri and Shortcuts** — home and Lock Screen widgets, a Control Center control, ask Siri how your agents are doing or send Claude an instruction, in Siri and Shortcuts. - 🔎 **Spotlight and Focus** — find past turns in Spotlight; a Focus filter shows only the agents waiting for you. - 📊 **Your services up close** — GitHub, Vercel, Stripe, Cal.com, n8n, Notion, Resend: your Mac reads their APIs with the keys in its Keychain and the iPhone shows the figures and lists. Safe actions (re-run CI, redeploy, merge a PR, pause a workflow) behind Face ID; nothing that moves money or sends an email. - 🫧 **Liquid Glass, native to the bone** — SwiftUI, tabs, zoom transitions, context menus, swipe actions, alternate icons, Mochi at 120 Hz. - 🔒 **Through your own iCloud** — sessions sync through your private CloudKit database; project names, commands and questions are encrypted with your iCloud keys. No Coucou server sees your projects, commands or keys. Turn it on in the Mac app: Settings → General → iPhone. **Get it on your iPhone in 3 steps:** install Coucou on your iPhone ([Join the TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/3GpeHv2b) — free, App Store coming soon), turn on **Settings → General → iPhone** in the Mac app (0.1.9 or later), and use the same Apple Account in iCloud on both. Full guide, troubleshooting and build-it-yourself: [docs/IPHONE.md](docs/IPHONE.md). ## Coucou for Android **Coucou for Android** brings Mochi to Android phones. It was built by [Rhytam Biswas (@Rhytam23)](https://github.com/Rhytam23) and lives in [`android/`](android/). - 🔐 **Approve from your phone** — a permission request rises over any screen, even on a locked phone; **Allow** needs your fingerprint or screen lock, **Deny** doesn't. A command too long to show in full can only be allowed on the computer. - 🧑‍💻 **Your agents at a glance** — the agent that needs you, the others below, plan usage and your services when the computer shares them. - 💬 **Answers and chat** — answer Claude Code's questions and chat through the computer's own AI keys (the keys never leave the computer). - 🏝️ **An island over other apps** *(optional)* — a black island drops from the camera cut-out while an agent works, plus a quick-settings tile and an ongoing notification. - 🧩 **Home-screen widgets** — nine of them, from a tiny Mochi to a big card with plan usage and quick buttons. Orange when something waits for you, blue while it works, green when it's done. Read-only: a request is always decided in the app. - 🔒 **Local and private** — the phone talks straight to your computer on your Wi-Fi, paired with a QR code and a pinned certificate. The phone link is **off by default**, and nothing listens until you turn it on. **Status:** tested on a real phone (Android 13) with the Windows app. The phone link is in **Coucou 0.4.0 for Windows and Linux**. Download the signed APK from the [latest Android release](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou/releases/tag/android-v0.3.0). Android needs Coucou on **Windows or Linux** (not the Mac), Android 11 or later, and both on the same Wi-Fi. Full guide: [`android/README.md`](android/README.md).

It builds Coucou from source on your machine, so the first build takes a while (about 20 minutes on a laptop, mostly Rust). **Try it** without installing anything: ```bash nix run github:Louis-CFM/coucou ``` Flakes not turned on yet? Add `--extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes'` after `nix`. **Install it** from your system flake: ```nix { inputs = { nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable"; coucou.url = "github:Louis-CFM/coucou"; }; outputs = { nixpkgs, coucou, ... }: { nixosConfigurations.my-machine = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { modules = [ ./configuration.nix ({ pkgs, ... }: { environment.systemPackages = [ coucou.packages.${pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.system}.default ]; }) ]; }; }; } ``` Then `sudo nixos-rebuild switch`. With Home Manager, the same package goes in `home.packages`. To build it against your own nixpkgs rather than the one pinned in Coucou's `flake.lock`, add `coucou.inputs.nixpkgs.follows = "nixpkgs";` (the flake is tested with nixos-unstable). **Or through the overlay**, as `pkgs.coucou`. Your nixpkgs then has to allow it (see *License* below): ```nix nixpkgs.overlays = [ coucou.overlays.default ]; nixpkgs.config.allowUnfreePredicate = pkg: builtins.elem (lib.getName pkg) [ "coucou" ]; environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.coucou ]; ``` **Update** with `nix flake update coucou`, then rebuild. The input follows `main`; to stay on releases, point it at a tag instead, like `github:Louis-CFM/coucou/linux-v0.6.0` (from the first release that has the flake). Coucou's own update card only links to the release page on Linux, so it never touches your system. **Good to know** - **License.** The package is marked unfree: the code is MIT, but the name, Mochi, the icon and the sounds are not (see [LICENSE-ASSETS.md](LICENSE-ASSETS.md)). Building it for yourself is allowed, which is what the flake does; it also keeps Coucou off public binary caches. The flake's `packages` allow it on their own; with the overlay, your config decides. - **Claude Code hooks** work as on any Linux. Coucou copies its relay to `~/.local/share/coucou/bin/` at each launch, so the hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` keep working across updates and garbage collections. **Start at login** and the shortcut commands in Settings use `coucou` from your `PATH`, for the same reason. - **API keys** go to the Secret Service. GNOME and Plasma have one; on Hyprland, Sway and other window managers, add `services.gnome.gnome-keyring.enable = true;`. - **On Wayland**, Flow dictation and global shortcuts go through `xdg-desktop-portal`, which the NixOS GNOME, Plasma and Hyprland modules turn on for you. - **The tray icon on GNOME** needs the AppIndicator extension: add `pkgs.gnomeExtensions.appindicator` and turn it on in Extensions. Without it, launch Coucou again to open its window. - **WhatsApp.** *Install WhatsApp* downloads GOWA's build for generic Linux. If it doesn't start (the dot stays grey and `~/.local/share/coucou/coucou.log` says `GOWA could not start`), add `programs.nix-ld.enable = true;` so programs built for other distributions can run. ### Build from source **macOS** — requirements: macOS 15+, Xcode 16+, [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen). ```bash brew install xcodegen git clone https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou.git cd coucou/NotchBuddy xcodegen open NotchBuddy.xcodeproj # then ⌘R ``` **Windows** — requirements: [Rust](https://rustup.rs), Node 20+, MSVC build tools. ```powershell git clone https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou.git cd coucou/windows npm install npm run pack # installer lands in windows/release/ ``` **Linux** — requirements: [Rust](https://rustup.rs), Node 20+, and the WebKitGTK, gtk-layer-shell and appindicator development packages (Debian/Ubuntu names below). ```bash sudo apt install build-essential pkg-config \ libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-layer-shell-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev \ librsvg2-dev libssl-dev libdbus-1-dev patchelf \ gstreamer1.0-plugins-base gstreamer1.0-plugins-good git clone https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou.git cd coucou/windows npm install npm run pack # AppImage, .deb and .rpm land in windows/release/ ``` On NixOS, `nix develop` gives you all of this: then `cd windows && npm ci && npm run tauri dev`. **Android** — requirements: JDK 17 and the Android SDK (platform 35). ```bash git clone https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou.git cd coucou/android ./gradlew assembleDebug # the APK lands in app/build/outputs/apk/debug/ ``` ## Setup On the Mac, open Coucou from the Dock or the menu bar: its window has every setting under **Notch** (⌘,). experimental)* | your WhatsApp messages in the notch or the island, and replies | Settings → Integrations → WhatsApp · a gateway on your Mac, see [WhatsApp (experimental)](#whatsapp-experimental) | If Coucou isn't running, the hook exits immediately: **Claude Code is never blocked.** ### WhatsApp (experimental) *macOS (GitHub build), and Windows and Linux since 0.5.3.* The WhatsApp pill shows your incoming messages in the notch, one row per conversation, and lets you reply without opening WhatsApp. WhatsApp has no API for personal accounts, so Coucou goes through an **unofficial gateway that runs on your Mac** and speaks the WhatsApp Web protocol: [GOWA](https://github.com/aldinokemal/go-whatsapp-web-multidevice) (recommended) or [OpenWA](https://github.com/rmyndharis/OpenWA). Coucou only reads and sends through that gateway. > **Unofficial.** Use it on your own account only. WhatsApp may restrict an account that abuses it (bulk messages, automation). Coucou only replies in a conversation that wrote to you, a few messages a minute at most. **Set it up in three steps, no Terminal:** 1. **Turn it on.** In Coucou: Settings → Integrations → WhatsApp (experimental) → **Show my WhatsApp messages**. 2. **Click Install WhatsApp.** Coucou downloads [GOWA](https://github.com/aldinokemal/go-whatsapp-web-multidevice), the open-source gateway, from its GitHub releases (the build for your Mac, about 15 MB, once), checks it against the SHA-256 GOWA publishes, and starts it. It starts and stops with Coucou from then on. 3. **Scan the QR code** that shows right there: on your phone, WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device. The dot turns green and the pill fills in as messages arrive. The gateway lives in `~/Library/Application Support/Coucou/GOWA`, next to the WhatsApp session it keeps, so you scan once. **Update** in the same place gets GOWA's latest version. That download is the only time Coucou goes online for WhatsApp, and only when you click. On Windows it lives in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Coucou\GOWA`, on Linux in `~/.local/share/coucou/GOWA`. Coucou tells the gateway where to post new messages (a small server on `127.0.0.1`, port 47823 by default, never reachable from another machine), with a random secret kept in the Keychain; every delivery is checked against its HMAC-SHA256 signature. If no message comes that way, Coucou checks every 20 seconds instead.
Advanced: run the gateway yourself (GOWA by hand, or OpenWA) Everything below is under **Advanced: your own gateway** in the same Settings section. **GOWA by hand.** Download `whatsapp__darwin_arm64.zip` (Apple silicon) or `…_darwin_amd64.zip` (Intel) from the [latest release](https://github.com/aldinokemal/go-whatsapp-web-multidevice/releases/latest). The zip holds one binary, `darwin-arm64` or `darwin-amd64`. In the folder it unzipped to: ```bash xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./darwin-arm64 ``` ```bash chmod +x ./darwin-arm64 ``` ```bash ./darwin-arm64 rest --host=127.0.0.1 --port=3000 --auto-download-media=false ``` Add `--basic-auth=user:password` to protect it with a password, and put the same `user:password` in Coucou. Keep `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, **Save**, then **Test connection**. The address and the password go to the Keychain. **OpenWA instead.** Start it with the Baileys engine and allow its webhook to reach your Mac, then pick **OpenWA** with `http://127.0.0.1:2785` and its API key (`data/.api-key` on first start): ```bash ENGINE_TYPE=baileys SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS=127.0.0.1 npm run start:prod ```
**What it does** - One row per conversation: initials, name, the last message cut short, the unread count. Photos, voice messages and documents show as a label (« Photo », « Voice message », « Document »); nothing is downloaded. - A new message: Mochi's little happy face, a sound if sounds are on, and the island opens under its usual rules. - Click a conversation: its last ten messages and a reply field. Return sends, Shift-Return starts a new line, Esc goes back. - Read receipts only when you open a conversation (or, if you turn that off, only when you reply). Never when a message just arrives. - Groups stay quiet unless you're mentioned; chats you ignore never show (right-click a row, or Settings); quiet during a macOS Focus when the system lets Coucou read it. **Privacy.** Coucou talks only to the gateway on your Mac (and to GitHub when you click Install or Update, to fetch GOWA itself). Messages stay in memory, are never written to disk or to a log, and are forgotten when Coucou quits or WhatsApp is turned off. No profile photo is fetched: they live on WhatsApp's servers, so the pill shows initials. **Limits.** No profile photos, no voice-message duration (neither gateway gives it), no new conversations from Coucou, no media sending. The gateway must run for messages to arrive. Following a Focus needs Coucou to be signed with Apple's Communication Notifications capability; until then that setting says it's unavailable. ### Supported agents | Agent | How it connects (Mac) | Mac-only? | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | Settings → Claude Code → **Install hooks** | No | | Gemini CLI | Settings → Gemini CLI → **Install hooks** | No | | Antigravity | Settings → Antigravity → **Install hooks** | No | | Cursor | Hooks installed automatically alongside Claude Code | No | | Codex | `--agent codex` flag; Settings → Codex → **Install hooks** | No | | Copilot CLI | `--agent copilot` flag + camelCase events | No | | Muse Code | `--agent muse` flag | No | | OpenCode | Plugin — **Settings → OpenCode Plugin → Install** | No | | Amp | Plugin — **Settings → Amp Plugin → Install** | No | | Hermes | Plugin — **Settings → Agents → Hermes → Install** | No | | Any other | `--agent ` flag; see [`docs/AGENTS.md`](docs/AGENTS.md) | No | OpenCode, Amp and Hermes use a plugin model rather than a hook command. Coucou installs the plugin file into `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`, `~/.config/amp/plugins/` and `~/.hermes/plugins/coucou/` respectively. On Windows and Linux the plugins start the `coucou-hook` relay directly — see [`windows/README.md`](windows/README.md#supported-agents). Agents running on a server (VS Code Remote - SSH, an SSH environment in the Claude app, Codex on a dev box) can reach Coucou on your Mac through an SSH tunnel: see [`docs/REMOTE.md`](docs/REMOTE.md). ## Things to try | Do this | Mochi does that | |---|---| | Hover the notch (top edge on Windows and Linux) | peeks out and says hi 👋 | | Click it | opens | | Hover Mochi | blinks, eyes grow | | Click Mochi | squish + annoyed | | Click 3 times fast | 😵‍💫 dizzy for a few seconds | | Drag a file onto the island | turns into a box and swallows it | | Drag Mochi onto a window *(macOS)* | attaches it as context | | Click the model name above the chat box *(macOS)* | switch AI provider or model | | Say « OK Coucou, play some music » *(macOS)* | listens, thinks, and does it | | Hold right ⌥ and speak, in any app *(macOS)* | Mochi listens in the pill, your words are pasted | | Hover the pill at the bottom of the screen *(macOS)* | opens a toolbar: dictate, record a call, open Coucou | ## How it works **macOS** - **Island**: a borderless `NSPanel` hugging the notch, driven by a small state machine (`hidden → petit → home`). - **Character**: drawn in SwiftUI `Canvas` + `TimelineView` at 60 fps — squircle body, eyes projected on a sphere, spring animations. No Rive, no Lottie, no images. - **Claude Code**: a tiny `nb-hook` script receives hook events and forwards them over a Unix socket to the app. For approvals it waits for your click, then answers the hook. - **Integrations**: lightweight pollers, paused when nothing is watching. - **Declared pills**: `PillCatalog.swift` is the single source of truth — every pill (coding tools, agents, AI providers, services) is declared there with its ID, color and category. - **Sounds**: 28 short WAVs played through preloaded `AVAudioPlayer`s. The macOS app is native Swift 6 / SwiftUI / AppKit with **zero third-party dependencies**. **iPhone** - A native SwiftUI app sharing Mochi's engine, the pills and the diff engine with the Mac through `CoucouKit`. - The Mac publishes sessions, turns and services to a private CloudKit zone in your iCloud (sensitive fields encrypted with your iCloud keys); the iPhone reads them and writes back decisions, answers and instructions, which the Mac only applies when they match what it is waiting on. - Live Activities are started and updated by APNs pushes through [`relay/`](relay/), a stateless Cloudflare Worker that holds the APNs key and only sees the agent's name and state. **Windows** - A [Tauri 2](https://tauri.app) app (Rust + TypeScript): the island is a transparent, always-on-top window that never steals focus, Mochi is drawn in Canvas 2D with the same shapes, timings and sounds as on the Mac. - Claude Code hooks go through a tiny `coucou-hook.exe` and a named pipe; keys live in Windows Credential Manager. - Details and differences in [`windows/README.md`](windows/README.md). **Linux** - The same Tauri app as Windows. On Wayland the island is a gtk-layer-shell overlay anchored to the top edge, and click-through is its input region. - Claude Code hooks go through the same `coucou-hook`, over a Unix socket in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`; keys live in the Secret Service. **Android** - A native Kotlin and Jetpack Compose app; Mochi is drawn in code, ported from the Windows app, with his outfits and sounds. - The phone link (`windows/src-tauri/src/phone_link`) is an opt-in server in the Windows and Linux app, on your local network only: TLS with a certificate pinned at pairing, a pairing code that "Pair again" replaces (and disconnects every phone), and approvals bound to the exact request the computer is waiting on. The protocol is in [`docs/ANDROID_LINK.md`](docs/ANDROID_LINK.md). ## Contributing Issues and PRs are very welcome — new integrations, new emotes, new sounds, bug fixes. # Coucou personalizado — Windows

Este pacote contem CODIGO-FONTE modificado. Nao e um instalador compilado.
O instalador original enviado nao foi alterado. Licencas e creditos originais foram preservados.

## O que foi preparado

- Chat como tela inicial da ilha. Pedidos de permissao pendentes continuam tendo prioridade.
- WhatsApp: conversa com mais espaco, fonte maior, horarios e ate 50 mensagens recentes.
  Ao abrir uma conversa, o painel usa sua largura para a leitura; Voltar retorna a lista e as integracoes.
- Botao Abrir midia para fotos, figurinhas, audio e video. Fotos/figurinhas podem ser ampliadas
  dentro do painel; audio/video usam controles nativos. Nao ha reproducao automatica.
  Este recurso de midia usa GOWA; OpenWA continua com as mensagens de texto e rotulos.
  Depende de a mensagem/midia ainda estar disponivel no gateway e de codecs do WebView2.
  Limite de 24 MiB por arquivo. Documentos, envio de anexos e gravacao de audio nao foram implementados.
  O download e solicitado ao GOWA so ao clicar. O GOWA pode manter o arquivo em statics/media;
  a interface do Coucou o mantem em memoria enquanto a conversa esta aberta.
- Controle de arrastar no cabecalho (simbolo de pontos): move horizontalmente e salva a posicao.
  Dois cliques centralizam; com o controle focado, setas movem e Home centraliza.
  Abra a ilha para acessar esse controle. O mascote continua com o gesto proprio dele.
- Importar conversa no chat: escolha .txt ou .md (ate 100 KB). Copie uma conversa ou um resumo
  do ChatGPT para um desses arquivos. O conteudo sera enviado ao provedor selecionado junto
  com sua proxima mensagem, e entra no contexto dessa conversa do Coucou.
  Clique no nome para remover antes de enviar. Limpar o chat tambem remove a importacao pendente.
  Nao ha sincronizacao automatica com o historico do ChatGPT nem acesso por usar a mesma conta.
  Nao importa automaticamente o ZIP/JSON da exportacao completa do ChatGPT.

## Atualizacoes por hotfix — sem reinstalar

As telas ficam embutidas no executavel do Tauri. Por isso ate uma mudanca de interface precisa
ser compilada, mas o usuario recebe um ZIP de hotfix com os binarios necessarios, sem reinstalar
ou refazer login/configuracoes. O app precisa ser fechado e aberto novamente.
Nao e atualizacao instantanea em tempo real nem atualizador remoto automatico.

O aplicador:
1. Verifica os SHA256 dos arquivos do pacote.
2. Localiza a instalacao (ou aceita -InstallDir).
3. Pede para fechar o Coucou.
4. Prepara os novos arquivos e copia os antigos para .coucou-hotfix-backups dentro da instalacao.
5. Substitui apenas coucou.exe e/ou coucou-hook.exe. Nao edita dados de conta, conversas ou configuracoes.
6. Se uma copia falhar, tenta restaurar os arquivos que substituiu.

Extraia o ZIP COMPLETO do hotfix. No PowerShell aberto na pasta extraida:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Aplicar-Hotfix.ps1
```

O Bypass acima vale somente para esse processo; nao altera a politica permanente do Windows.
Se a instalacao nao for detectada ou houver mais de uma:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\Aplicar-Hotfix.ps1 -InstallDir "C:\caminho\do\Coucou"
```

Instalacoes MSI em uma pasta protegida podem exigir abrir o PowerShell como administrador.
Se houver erro depois de abrir a nova versao, feche o Coucou e copie os .exe do backup mais recente
sobre os arquivos da pasta de instalacao. O rollback automatico cobre falhas de copia, nao falhas
funcionais detectadas depois. Nao apague os backups antes de validar a nova versao.
Os hashes conferem integridade; use apenas pacotes de origem confiavel.
Atualizacoes oficiais do Coucou podem substituir esta personalizacao.

## Gerar um hotfix no Windows

Instale Node.js 24 LTS (https://nodejs.org), Rust (https://rustup.rs) e Visual Studio Build Tools
com a carga Desktop development with C++ e Windows SDK. Reinicie o terminal apos instalar.
WebView2 tambem e necessario para executar o aplicativo.

Na pasta windows deste projeto:

```powershell
npm ci
npm run hotfix
```

O pacote fica em windows/release/hotfix-custom-.../. Compacte o conteudo dessa pasta em ZIP.
O comando compila sem gerar instalador NSIS/MSI. Na primeira atualizacao, ele inclui os dois .exe.
Nas seguintes, para incluir apenas os binarios realmente diferentes de uma compilacao anterior:

```powershell
npm run tauri build -- --no-bundle
node scripts/hotfix.mjs --base "C:\pasta\dos\binarios\anteriores"
```

A pasta --base precisa conter os .exe antigos, nao o ZIP deles.
A versao base continua sendo 0.5.9; cada pacote tem uma revisao custom com data no manifesto.
Esse formato deve ser revisto se futuras mudancas adicionarem recursos nativos alem desses dois .exe.

## Alternativa: compilar no GitHub

Em um repositorio seu com este projeto, a acao Coucou - hotfix personalizado pode ser executada
manualmente em Actions. Ela compila no Windows, executa os testes e entrega o artefato
Coucou-Hotfix-Windows. Nao publica releases nem modifica sua instalacao automaticamente.
A primeira execucao pode demorar; seguintes aproveitam o cache de compilacao.
O workflow foi preparado, mas ainda nao executado neste ambiente.

## Validacao

Veja VALIDACAO.txt para os resultados locais e o que ainda depende do Windows.

## Nome personalizado

Em Ajustes > Geral > Nome do assistente, escolha ate 32 caracteres e clique Salvar nome.
O nome aparece na interface, titulos, menu da bandeja e identidade do chat. A chamada de voz
usa OK seguido do nome escolhido (por exemplo, OK Jarvis). O reconhecimento depende do Parakeet
transcrever esse nome; nomes de varias palavras sao aceitos. O nome padrao preserva as variantes
de pronuncia de Coucou. Para perceber a identidade nova no chat, inicie uma conversa nova.

No Windows tambem e criado um alias .cmd com o nome em minusculas (acentos normalizados e
espacos substituidos por hifens), na pasta aliases dos dados do aplicativo. A configuracao mostra
o comando completo para PowerShell. O alias encaminha argumentos, inclusive --shortcut.
Nomes reservados do Windows recebem o prefixo app-. O alias nao e adicionado ao PATH global.
Os nomes tecnicos coucou.exe/coucou-hook.exe, identificador de instalacao e caminhos existentes
continuam estaveis para preservar hotfixes, hooks e dados. Os creditos/licencas originais permanecem.

name: Coucou - hotfix personalizado
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: windows
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: windows/package-lock.json
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            windows/target
          key: custom-hotfix-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('windows/Cargo.lock') }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx tsc --noEmit
      - run: node --import ./tests/setup.mjs --test --test-force-exit --test-timeout=20000 "tests/**/*.test.mjs"
      - run: cargo build --release --locked -p coucou-hook
      - run: npm run hotfix
      - run: cargo test --workspace --locked
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: Coucou-Hotfix-Windows
          path: windows/release/hotfix-*/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
